articleTitle: Covers
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: diffraction; wave propagation; interference head wave; electron scattering; nanoelectronic device; resonators; and waveguides.

articleTitle: Boundary layer approach to construct an interference head wave
abstract: The paper concerns high-frequency scalar diffraction on a contact of two acoustic media with different velocities of propagation. Attention is focused on the boundary layer in a neighborhood of the point of incidence of the limiting ray and on the interference head wave formed by the whispering gallery wave.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic surface waves guided by the metal-composite medium boundary
abstract: The possibility of the existence of electromagnetic surface waves guided by the composite medium-metal planer boundary is investigated. It is shown that the parametric interaction of these waves in the presence of an external time-harmonic electromagnetic field can be observed. The expression of growth rate for the surface-wave amplitudes is determined.

articleTitle: Wigner distribution function and intensity integral moments of Hermite-Laguerre-Gaaussian beams
abstract: Hermite-Laguerre-Gaussian (HLG) beams are recently introduced light beam family that contains Hermite-Gaussian and Laguerre-Gaussian beams as particular representatives. The Wigner function and some other integral characteristics for HLG beams are found and discussed.

articleTitle: On the asymptotics of Rayleigh type waves for singular propagation directions on the surface of anisotropic elastic body
abstract: The general method [1,2] for construction of uniform asymptotics for surface waves in an anisotropic elastic media is employed in the special cases where the velocities (we mean here the phase velocities) of two quasi-shear waves turn out to be coincident at certain points on the boundary surface S.

articleTitle: Biot's equations for multiphase media with temperature gradient on the basis of generalized variational principle
abstract: The system of generalized Biot's equations, describing waves propagation in a multi-phase or multi- component medium in the presence of heat exchange between phases, is derived on the basis of generalized variational principle [Maximov G.A. DD2006, p. 173-177]. It is shown that in the presence of N phases 2N propagating eigen-modes can exist in this medium. At high frequencies N modes are of the mechanical (acoustical) type and N modes are of the diffusive (thermal) type of propagation. At low frequencies there is the single acoustical (wave) mode and the rest 2N-1 modes possess the diffusion (thermal) type of behavior. For a two-component medium without temperature exchange the developed approach is reduced to the well known Biot's model. The account of the temperature field yields the generalized Biot's model for two components medium.

articleTitle: Diffractive model of scattering by a rough surface
abstract: A diffractive model of spatial distribution of radiation scattered by a rough surface is proposed. The following angular dependencies are presented: - intensity of scattered radiation; - spatial frequency spectrum of fluctuations of the scattered field (static speckle-structure); - time frequency spectrum of intensity fluctuations of the radiation scattered by a moving surface (dynamic speckle-structure). The applicability of the proposed model for various wavelengths and objects types is experimentally confirmed.

articleTitle: Diffraction of surface waves on the line of velocity discontinuity
abstract: A problem of diffraction of waves on a vertical interface of media is studied. The waves are radiated by a point source. The reflected and transmitted wave fields are obtained by the method of parabolic equation. The corresponding transformation coefficients are found for the Neumann boundary condition.

articleTitle: Smoothed Wigner transforms and homogenization of wave propagation
abstract: The Wigner transform (WT) is a well known quadratic transform, mapping a wavefunction to a position-wavenumber quasi-density. WTs are used in the asymptotic treatment of semiclassical and other wave problems. The smoothed WT (SWT) method is a regularization and extension of WT-based approaches for the homogenization of wave propagation, which decouples homogenization from asymptotics: exact equations for the evolution of a given problem at coarse scale can be obtained, instead of merely looking at small parameter limits. In this work we present the derivation of the SWT equations.

articleTitle: Electron scattering by nanotube Y-junction. Computation and application to modeling by graphs
abstract: We demonstrate a possibility to compute the intensity of electron transport through Y-type junctions of three-dimensional metallic nanotubes. Keeping in mind an asymptotic modeling of reliable nanostructures by quantum graphs, we conjecture that scattering matrix of a graph should be the same as scattering matrix of its nanosize-prototype. The numerical computation of the latter allows a way to determine the "gluing" conditions at a graph. Exploring this conjecture we show that commonly used gluing conditions for graphs are normally not adequate.

articleTitle: On gyroscopic effects in vibrating and axially rotating solid and annular discs
abstract: "Bryan's effect" - that is, the effect of a vibrating pattern's precession in the direction of inertial rotation of a vibrating ring - was discovered by G. Bryan in 1890. This effect has several applications in navigational instruments, such as cylindrical, hemispherical and planar circular disc rotational sensors. The model of a thin circular disc vibrating in its plane and subjected to inertial rotation is considered. The dynamics of the disc gyroscope are considered in terms of linear elasticity. Two models are considered: solid discs and a composite disc consisting of concentric annular discs with various boundary conditions on the inner and outer circumferences. It is assumed that the angular rate of inertial rotation of the composite disc is constant and has axial orientation. It is also assumed that this angular rate is much smaller than the lowest eigenvalue of the composite disk. Hence any centrifugal effects and quantities that are proportional to the square of the angular rate are negligible. Our model is formulated in general terms and then compared to a formulation in terms of Novozhilov-Arnold-Warbur-ton's theory of thin shells. The system of equations of motion of the disc is separated and transformed into a pair of wave equations in polar coordinates. A solution is obtained in terms of Bessel and Neumann functions. Various non-axisymmetric modes of the composite disc are considered and the dependence of Bryan's effect on eigenvalues, mass densities of the composite disc, its modulii of elasticity, Poisson ratios, outer and inner radii of the disc, and for various types of boundary conditions, are investigated.

articleTitle: Features of propagation and interaction of one-dimensional topological solitons in crystals
abstract: In the present work the interaction of two similar solitons (Frenkel-Kontorova dislocations) has been considered at their combined motion at the same speed in one gliding plane.Based on a numerical experiment for soliton solutions of the nonlinear sinus- Gordon wave equation,the following results were obtained: the interaction between the dislocations proved important at low velocities; the displacement field of some given dislocation was strongly distorted under the action of neighboring dislocation. In our opinion, in this case a transverse slide of the dislocation in question is observed. The interaction force between these dislocations decreases with increasing velocity and in the limit when the dislocation velocity tends to the velocity of sound,the interaction between the dislocations tends to zero. It was then obtained that the behavior of dislocation motion depended upon the height of periodical potential barrier of crystal lattice.In case of low barriers the motion is translational.In high barrier crystals the dislocation as if executes oscillating motion in the direction of slide. The tail-end ranges of dislocations are distorted.The width of dislocation periodically changes remaining all the time less than that in low barrier crystals.

articleTitle: On uniqueness in the two-and three-dimensional Neumann-Kelvin problem
abstract: The uniqueness question for the classical Neumann-Kelvin problem of the linear theory of ship waves is considered. Both two- and three-dimensional problems are studied in the case when contours of ships are totally submerged. A new uniqueness theorem, valid for bodies of arbitrary shape and without assumptions on finiteness of energy, is proved. Simple bounds for the set of parameters, for which non- uniqueness can occur, are found.

articleTitle: Numerical estimation of acoustic properties in enclosures of simple shape
abstract: A 2-D model of a rectangular room with an open window is studied. In such a room the acoustic field is not diffuse even for high frequencies. Instead, it displays modal properties in the whole frequency band. For high frequency some modes have a high Q-factor, and thus the solution of a harmonic excitation problem has a rapid and unpredictable dependence on frequency. To suppress this dependence, a procedure of averaging in the frequency domain is proposed. An algorithm of calculation of reverberation time is described.

articleTitle: Mathematical model and design of nanoeloctronic device based on metal-dielectric transition
abstract: A new type of nanoelectronic device based on stimulated Peierls-Mott transition is studied analytically and numerically. By means of conformal mappings a quantum mechanical potential for ballistic electrons moving on the conducting electrode has been calculated in terms of elliptic functions. The latter are parameterized by the geometrical characteristics of the nano-device and the governing voltage applied. The spectral zone structure of the effective Schrodinger operator has been calculated numerically for various sets of the device parameters. For the device fabricated from GaAs semiconductor the set of parameters which guarantee the stable metal-dielectric transition at liquid helium temperature has been found.

articleTitle: Numerical approach for analysis of surface wave field in the vicinity of caustics
abstract: Due to lateral heterogeneity of upper part of the Earth surface waves paths deviate from great circle arcs that result in appearance of caustics at the hemisphere opposite to the epicenter. The caustics have a shape of cusps, and they may superpose. Asymptotic approach for analysis of the wave field in the vicinity of such caustics is reduced to calculation of the Pearcey integral, whose parameters are determined through the eikonals of three superposed waves. Calculation of surface wave field on the basis of the asymptotic approach has some drawbacks and cannot be applied to superposition of caustics. We propose a numerical approach for calculation of the field using the Green formula. It is reduced to calculation of an integral with oscillating integrand. A method for suppression of oscillation of the integral is outlined. For a simple model asymptotic and numerical approaches are in a good agreement. Some examples of calculation for different shape of caustics on spherical surface are given.

articleTitle: Pulsed radiation produced by a travelling exponentially decaying bipolar current pulse with high-frequency filling
abstract: Electromagnetic waves accompanying high-frequency modulated current pulses, exponentially decaying with time and travelling without losses along a line segment of a finite length, are investigated for both subluminal and luminal velocities of the pulse propagation.

articleTitle: Windowed oscillatory integral: an approach to compute high-frequency wave fields
abstract: We revise known approaches to compute high- frequency wave-fields and propose a new one. The approach is uniform in the sense that, in contrary to the conventional ray-tracing method, it can be applied globally and independently of ray-field singularities (caustics). The obtained representation has the form of an integral over rays, only rays passing through a vicinity of the observation point contribute. The integral representation differs, however, from analogous ones (such as Maslov's canonical operator and Gaussian-beams method) and provides efficient tool for computation of electromagnetic, acoustic and elastic high-frequency waves.

articleTitle: On similarity between superluminal current pulse shape and time derivative of Whittaker potential
abstract: In this work the calculation of derivative of Whittaker potential υ with respect to τ was performed in the framework of linear current model. Results of computation have shown similarity of the form of the superluminal running current pulse on one hand and the derivative of Whittaker potential ∂υ/∂τ on the other in far region at Cherenkov angle.

articleTitle: Whispering gallery eigenmodes of a surface with anisotropic surface impedance
abstract: Problem of finding electromagnetic whispering gallery eigenmodes of a three-dimensional curvilinear surface is considered. It is assumed that the wavelength of the eigenmodes is much smaller than principal radii of curvature of the surface (high frequency approximation). It is also assumed that electromagnetic field satisfy anisotropic impedance boundary conditions on the surface. The problem is solved in torsionless approximation using both the perturbation method and the method of reference problem.

articleTitle: Justification of the asymptotic solutions of linear system with a turning point of high order
abstract: In the present paper justification of the asymptotic solutions of linear system with a high-order turning point constructed is proved.

articleTitle: Universality of Feigenbaum and dissipative microstructures for highly nonequilibrium nonlinear systems
abstract: The effect of steplike change of spatial period of resonant relief on the condensed matter surfaces and in the volume under the action of intense laser radiation was investigated. The effect was observed in wide range of laser radiation duration's from continuous wave one to the femtosecond. The effect was observed for materials with different properties from dielectrics and semiconductors to metals. The physical cause of remnant structures formation is the interference of incident wave with excited by it surface electromagnetic modes and are in the frameworks of universal polaritonic model of matter damage. It is shown that the formation of remnant structures with two or three values of spatial multiple periods are in framework of universal polaritonic model of condensed matter damage. The interpretation of the micro- and nanostructures formation in system intense laser radiation interacted with solid state material and the regular structures formation was made based on mathematical model of Feigenbaum universality where the value proportional to the number of laser pulses is controlled (bifurcation) parameter.

articleTitle: The transient waves produced by hyperbolic motion of Gaussian's transverse sources
abstract: We consider two sub- and superluminal solutions of the wave equation. Possibilities of adequate description of the generated waves due to the transverse sources are discussed.

articleTitle: Solving the problems of diffraction by Wiener-Hopf-Fock method for finite fine structures
abstract: This paper deals with further development of Wiener-Hopf-Fock method for solving the wave's diffraction on fine strip-slotted structures problems. The classical problem on diffraction of plane wave on a strip is offered as a key problem. The boundary value problem is consecutively solved by reducing to the system of singular boundary integral equations, then to the system of the second kind Fredholm equations. The exact solution of the problem and asymptotic expressions for fields are found.

articleTitle: The scattering operator in the stepwise waveguides
abstract: We consider the mathematical model of the interface of two homogeneous waveguides. This model includes, as particular cases, most types of the acoustic, electrodynamic and quantum waveguide interfaces. We give an accurate mathematical construction of the most important object in the waveguide interface theory - the scattering operator and discuss its most general properties.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Faraday effect in open resonators
abstract: Enhancement of the Faraday effect in multilayer structures is considered. The structures are treated as open resonators. It is shown that the angle of Faraday rotation can be represented as a product of two factors, the first one is determined by the bulk magnetooptical properties and the second is a Q-factor of the resonator. The enhancement of MO properties is illustrated by consideration of the Airy's partial waves in single MO slab. This approach is generalized to an arbitrary MO resonant structure and allows us to design scheme with "perfect" Faraday effect with rotation by 90deg and unitary transmission..

articleTitle: Diffraction of 2D complex beams by a perfect conductor half-plane: a spectral approach
abstract: The incidence of a complex beam on a perfect conducting half-plane is analyzed by the method of the angular plane wave spectrum decomposition. The rigorous analysis of the integral representation of the solution allows to understand the field behaviour. The different contributions divide the observation space in regions where a given contribution is more significant.

articleTitle: Asymptotic solutions of some hyperbolic nonlinear equations
abstract: Nonlinear hyperbolic equations are considered. Some asymptotic and exact solutions of these equations are obtained.

articleTitle: PO\PTD near-field scattering and diffraction method for path loss prediction in urban mobile radio-systems
abstract: In this paper the 3-D mathematical formulation and study for the simulation of the radio-propagation mechanisms in urban cellular environments are presented. The proposed methods and techniques are applicable to the 3-D radiocoverage prediction model, currently being developed by the authors' research group. In the far field area, the proposed analysis is based on the well-known deterministic methods of Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD). In the near field and Frenel zone, a novel and time-efficient technique for the computation of the scattered and diffracted field is applied. Emphasis is also given to the time efficiency of the proposed approach since the high simulation time is one of the most important drawbacks of such radio-propagation prediction codes.

articleTitle: An attempt to improve semiclassical calculations of wave transport in a quantum wire with diffraction
abstract: In our previous presentations in the series of this seminar, we have shown an interesting phenomenon which was found numerically and later explained semiclassically for coherent electronic transmission through a mesoscopic quantum wire with a step structure: Fistly, we reported by our numerical work that the electric current shows periodic oscillations as a function of a system parameter; secondly, we presented its semiclassical description to explain analytically that this is purely the effect of diffraction and constructive interference of transmitting electrons at the step structure of the wire. This time, we further report an attempt to improve the semi- classical calculations of wave transport in such a system.

articleTitle: Excitation of whistler modes guided by a lossy anisotropic plasma column
abstract: A study is made of the excitation of electromagnetic waves by spatially bounded given electric currents in the presence of an axially magnetized cylindrical plasma column surrounded by free space. A rigorous solution for the total field comprising both the discrete and continuous parts of the spatial spectrum of the excited waves is found. Using the obtained field representation, the contributions of guided and unguided modes of the column to the impedance of a loop antenna are determined for the whistler frequency range. It is shown that allowance for relatively small collisional losses in the plasma can result in appreciable redistribution of the antenna- launched power among the excited modes.

articleTitle: The comparison of fields excited by input grating coupler with those of surface electromagnetic waves
abstract: The nature of the bulk near-surface light radiation arising in the conditions of surface electromagnetic wave excitation by finite-size input grating has been theoretically studied.
